output.brief: The evidence points mainly at Callerby, not Halden. The platform's tamper-proof records show the architect answered 62 of 64 questions on time. The two late ones were minor finishes queries in May 2026, and Callerby itself marked them as having no programme impact. 39 of the 41 "late" questions in your draft claim were sitting in Callerby's own draft folder for 9–47 days before they were sent. The tower crane left in October 2025 for Kestrel and came back in April. Steel erection restarted within days of its return. The site diaries only say "on hold – design" and never say what information was missing. So the CO-09 change order may have contributed, but I can't say how much. I'm fairly confident the RFI part of the claim fails and that the crane move was a major cause. I'm less sure about the change orders and about whether the incentive scheme drove the crane move. Next steps: don't submit the claim as drafted, because it rests on figures the platform contradicts. Get an independent delay analysis that uses the platform's timestamps and the crane ledger, and have it separate out any genuine CO-09 delay. Don't discipline the superintendent for answering honestly. Don't change the incentive scheme until the link to the crane move is shown. Review the claims consultant's contingent fee.
